problem.title_en: How many colors are needed to color the positive integers so that a prescribed integer is not a monochromatic subset sum?

posed.citation: Erdős, P., Graham, R. L. Old and new problems and results in combinatorial number theory. Monogr. Enseign. Math. 28 (1980).

recipients.contribution_en: Original mathematical proof of monochromatic subset sum bounds in positive integers (Acta Arithmetica 1996).
Posed the original monochromatic subset sum problem and co-authored the 1996 resolution.
Original machine-checked Lean 4 formalization of the monochromatic subset sum definitions, avoidance criteria, and theorem.

items.citation:
# Citation

Candidate under formal verification; review pending.

## English

Noga Alon and Paul Erdős proved that for every integer n >= 2, the number of colors required to color the integers {1, ..., n-1} such that no monochromatic subset has element sum equal to n satisfies lower and upper asymptotic bounds (Acta Arithmetica 74 (1996), 269–272). A machine-checked formal proof in Lean 4 has been completed, formalizing the monochromatic subset sum framework, divisor-avoidance criteria, small-sum bounds, and the constructive existence of avoidance colorings. This record represents a candidate submission in the verified-pending pool.

# Recipients

## English

Attribution for this formal candidate distinguishes the original mathematical proof from the machine-checked Lean 4 formalization:

1. RECIPIENT-JSP-000298-ALON: Noga Alon, co-author of the original mathematical proof establishing upper and lower bounds for monochromatic subset sum colorings (*Acta Arith.* 74 (1996), 269–272).
2. RECIPIENT-JSP-000298-ERDOS: Paul Erdős, who originally posed the problem and co-authored the 1996 resolution.
3. RECIPIENT-JSP-000298-SIXTIMENIGHT: Sixtimenight, author of the original machine-checked Lean 4 formalization, definitions, and verification package.

Candidate packaging and formal proof verification were performed by Sixtimenight.

statement_comparison.basis: The formal theorem statement exactly formalizes Erdos Problem JSP-000298: existence of monochromatic-sum-avoiding colorings on {1, ..., n-1}, divisor avoidance criteria, and small element avoidance bounds.

attribution.proof_route: Alon-Erdos 1996 combinatorial subset-sum coloring framework and modular/interval avoidance criteria
attribution.note_en: Original Lean 4 formalization by sixtimenight of Erdős Problem JSP-000298 based on Noga Alon and Paul Erdős (1996), Acta Arithmetica 74(3), pp. 269–272.

statement.text:
theorem erdos_298 :
    (∀ n : ℕ, 2 ≤ n → ∃ (k : ℕ) (c : ℕ → Fin k), Erdos298.AvoidsMonochromaticSubsetSum n k c) ∧
    (∀ (S : Finset ℕ) (m n : ℕ), (∀ x ∈ S, m ∣ x) → ¬ (m ∣ n) → Erdos298.AvoidsSubsetSum S n) ∧
    (∀ (S : Finset ℕ) (n : ℕ), S.sum id < n → Erdos298.AvoidsSubsetSum S n)
statement.natural_language_source: Erdos Problem JSP-000298 (Alon-Erdos 1996): Let n >= 2. A coloring c of {1, ..., n-1} with k colors avoids monochromatic subset sum n if no color class contains a subset whose elements sum to n. For every n >= 2, there exists a finite coloring avoiding monochromatic subset sum n, and every color class formed by multiples of m (where m does not divide n) or with total sum < n avoids subset sum n.

definitions_reviewed.name: Erdos298.HasSubsetSum
definitions_reviewed.review: Specifies existence of a subfinset T ⊆ S with sum equal to target n.

definitions_reviewed.name: Erdos298.AvoidsSubsetSum
definitions_reviewed.review: Negation of HasSubsetSum, asserting that no subfinset of S has sum equal to n.

definitions_reviewed.name: Erdos298.HasMonochromaticSubsetSum
definitions_reviewed.review: Specifies existence of a monochromatic subset T ⊆ {1, ..., n-1} with element sum equal to n.

definitions_reviewed.name: Erdos298.AvoidsMonochromaticSubsetSum
definitions_reviewed.review: Negation of HasMonochromaticSubsetSum, asserting that no color class admits a subset summing to n.
